gaps.sentence: The new stadium ___ by the end of the decade.
gaps.explanation: 'By the end of the decade' needs future perfect passive: will have been + completed. The stadium is completed by somebody.

gaps.sentence: The ambush ___ (plan) by someone with intimate knowledge of the valley.
gaps.explanation: Past perfect passive (had been planned) stresses completion before the ambush; was planned is also acceptable.

gaps.sentence: Over two hundred bird species ___ (record) in the valley this spring.
gaps.explanation: 'This spring' is an open time frame, so present perfect passive: have been + recorded.

gaps.sentence: The stairs ___ (reinforce) when part of the ceiling gave way.
gaps.hint: action in progress at a past moment
gaps.explanation: Past continuous passive: was/were being + past participle, interrupted by a sudden past event.

gaps.sentence: She couldn't pay because her wallet ___ (steal) at the market.
gaps.hint: earlier past action causing a past problem
gaps.explanation: The theft happened before the failed payment: past perfect passive, had been + stolen.

gaps.sentence: The parcels ___ (deliver) every morning before the shop opens.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive (am/is/are + past participle) for regular, repeated actions: are delivered.

gaps.sentence: The whole engine ___ (strip down) before the fault could be located.
gaps.explanation: Past necessity: had to be + stripped down (phrasal verbs passivise too, particle retained).

gaps.sentence: The debt ___ (repay) in full by May, he promised.
gaps.explanation: Reported future passive: would be + past participle after a past reporting verb.
